Listens by month

Every month since the first listen, one bar per month. Years alternate shades.
How this is counted
  • A listen is a play that lasted at least 30 seconds. Shorter plays (skips) are not in the data at all.
  • History starts in January 2018.
  • Live versions, remasters, radio and single edits, extended cuts, feat. and with tags, and Taylor's Versions count as the original song.
  • Remixes and acoustic versions stay separate songs. Podcasts and audiobooks are excluded.
  • Times are local: UTC-8 before August 1, 2021 and UTC-5 from then on, with no daylight saving. Years, months, days and hours all use this.
  • Everything is by calendar year. The export ends Nov 4, 2026, so 2026 is a partial year.
  • Hours are the time actually played. Album covers come from Spotify, artist photos from Deezer.

Top artists

Top songs

How this is counted
  • Spotify doesn't share genres for this app, so they come from Deezer, where every album has a genre.
  • Each listened album is matched to the artist's Deezer catalog by title. An artist's genre is the one that covers most of their listens; albums with no match count as the genre most of the artist's Deezer catalog has.
  • Every listen of an artist counts toward that one genre, so a pop song by a mostly hip-hop artist counts as hip-hop. The artist is the album artist.
  • Deezer genres are grouped into a dozen buckets (Electro and Dance become Electronic & Dance, R&B and Soul & Funk become R&B & Soul, and so on). Unknown means the artist wasn't found on Deezer.
  • The mix chart shows the top 10 genres in color; the rest are grouped into Other.

Lost favorites

Songs you fell for on their own and then lost: at least 20 all-time listens and not one in the last 18 months. The score is the listens in the song's busiest 90 days, times its share of everything you played by that artist (a song that carried the artist won't come back by playing the artist), times how long it's been quiet (full credit at 2 years). At most 2 songs per artist.
